subject: Privacy addendum - post-demo data handling & breach questions
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@carepathhealth.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@carepathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jan 2028 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Privacy addendum - post-demo data handling & breach questions

Hi Amit / Dana — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying asks so your legal/security team can move quickly on the addendum side. We covered a lot; below are the items we heard and what we can provide next: 

1) Roles: controller vs. processor
- Our default stance: customers act as Controller and Redwood acts as Processor for inference requests handled by the hosted/dedicated products. We can surface a short controller/processor addendum for signature.

2) Subprocessors
- You asked for a full inventory. Attached is a preview DPA and we can provide an up-to-date subprocessor CSV (we maintain an official list and a notification cadence).

3) Breach notification window
- Standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents. We understand some healthcare customers request shorter windows; please flag if CarePath needs a 48-hour requirement so I can escalate to our contracts team.

4) PII handling & retention
- Default log retention is 90 days; model input prefixes are not persisted beyond cache lifetimes unless you enable debug logs. We offer configurable retention on Dedicated/Private plans.

5) Data residency & encryption
- Regions available: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (if needed for EU). All traffic is TLS in transit; at-rest encryption is supported with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.

Action items from Redwood: please confirm your legal/security contact and whether you want the controller/processor addendum in Track Changes (Word) or as a proposed DocuSign. I attached a preview DPA (redwood-dpa-preview.pdf) for internal review.

Suggested next step: 30-min legal-to-legal on Wednesday to run through subprocessor list + SOC 2 evidence. Proposed times: Wed 10:00–11:00 ET or Thu 14:00–15:00 ET. 

Thanks — happy to tighten any of the language above.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: redwood-dpa-preview.pdf (PDF, 324 KB)
From: Amit Shah <amit@carepathhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@carepathhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jan 2028 11:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Privacy addendum - post-demo data handling & breach questions

Logan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the preview DPA: 

- Controller/Processor: CarePath will be the Controller for patient records we send for enrichment. We expect Redwood to be a Processor and to sign a standard C/P addendum.
- Subprocessors: we need the current list + a commitment to 30 days advance notice for any new subprocessor with the option to object for high-risk subprocessors.
- Breach window: because we operate under state-level breach rules and have internal SLAs, our security team prefers a 48-hour notification for confirmed unauthorized access to PHI. Is that something Redwood can commit to contractually?
- SOC 2: please provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a redaction-friendly summary if available.
- Encryption: confirm TLS1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest. Also confirm whether KV cache persists any identifiable values by default.

If you can provide answers and the subprocessors CSV, we will route to our contracts group. We are happy to do the proposed legal-to-legal call — Wed 10 ET works for us.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Security & Privacy, CarePath Health
amit@carepathhealth.com

Hi Amit — looping in a few technical specifics you asked about so your security team has concrete detail to review with contracts. I pulled these from our infra and compliance notes: 

- Breach notification: our operational SLA is to notify customers within 72 hours after confirming unauthorized access to customer data. For enterprise agreements we can discuss a 48-hour contractual window; that requires approval from Legal and Ops and a narrow definition of "confirmed access" in the addendum.

- Subprocessors (current snapshot):
  * CloudHost Inc. — hosting and physical infra (US regions)
  * FastQueue Ltd. — transient queuing/batching layer
  * MetricsHub — telemetry and product analytics (no customer text storage)

  We maintain an internal inventory and publish updates. We can provide a CSV export (attached). For high-risk objections we follow a remediation/alternative-provider discussion cadence.

- Logging & retention:
  * Default application logs: 90 days (configurable for Dedicated/Private)
  * Access logs/audit trails: 365 days (retained for compliance packages)
  * KV cache used for transformer keys is ephemeral and does not persist raw PII by default; customers can opt into debug logging which does persist additional context for troubleshooting (we disable by default).

- Encryption:
  * TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS.

Attachments: subprocessors-2028-01-30.csv (CSV, 8 KB)

Next steps proposer: Logan, can you share the SOC 2 report via a secure link and propose a legal-to-legal invite (Wed 10ET)? I’ll join to help clarify the logging/residency details.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Logan / Ben — that helps a lot. Two quick asks before we lock times with Contracts: 

1) Please share SOC 2 Type II report (redacted copy is fine) and the subprocessors CSV to privacy@carepathhealth.com.
2) Confirm whether Redwood is willing to sign a Controller/Processor addendum with a 48-hour notification term (we can include an exceptions clause for ongoing investigations). If Redwood cannot commit to 48 hours, please confirm the escalated SLA process and expected timeline to get approval.

We’ll tentatively accept Wed 10 ET for the legal-to-legal; please send an invite and include your contracts counsel and any security engineer who can speak to logs/retention.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,
Amit
Head of Security & Privacy, CarePath Health
